title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 21 | Week 7 vs. Denver Broncos
headline: Jeremiyah Love, Budda Baker and Jedrick Wills Jr. were all held out of Wednesday's practice; Love is improving but won't play until he's at 100%, with the rest of the week to be reevaluated day to day.
summary: LaFleur opened by saying Jeremiyah Love, Budda Baker and Jedrick Wills Jr. were out of Wednesday's practice, and that an illness was going around the building. He said the three will be reevaluated day to day, with Baker and Wills out today and a decision on tomorrow to follow. Love is feeling better, but LaFleur said he won't play him until he is fully healthy. He praised Darius Robinson's work ethic and coachability, and said his teammates clearly value him. On man coverage, LaFleur said there were missed chances to call better plays and some separations that weren't converted. He credited the offense's improving run game variety but said operation (cadence and snap execution) is the biggest area to fix, and that the goal is to be the league's best at those details. He defended burning a timeout late in the first half near the goal line, calling it a reasonable decision in a tough, somewhat unlucky spot. He described Denver's defense as well coached and old-school, and said they have been consistently strong for several years. On the red zone, he took responsibility for play design and clarity, said the offense has been decent there overall, and said the team needs to finish drives better. He also said the Denver defense is the next challenge.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Wednesday, October 21st | Press Conference
headline: Injury news is still fluid: Kendal Daniels (concussion) and AJ Terrell are both trending toward practice, Divine Deablo and C.J. Henderson are unclear, and Bijan Robinson's usage is getting emphasis before the 49ers game.
summary: Stefanski opened by saying the Falcons are working through injuries and that some players will practice this week while others won't, with no one ruled in or out yet. He called San Francisco undefeated for a reason and said Atlanta must play its best Sunday. Kendal Daniels is doing much better after a concussion and will practice Wednesday, while AJ Terrell will also practice today, though the coach would not yet judge his readiness for Sunday. He said Divine Deablo is improving but could not say what the next few days look like, and he was similarly vague on C.J. Henderson's status. On the offense, he said Bijan Robinson is guaranteed the ball on handoffs and that the staff will keep finding ways to use him in the run and pass game. He admitted the last game was poorly played and poorly coached, and said Jake Matthews is healthy. Zachariah Branch keeps his special teams role, and Charles Snowden was signed off the practice squad to add depth, with the staff seeing how quickly he can absorb the scheme this week.

title: Jesse Minter on Lamar Jackson's Health, Defensive Growth
headline: Lamar Jackson got limited work at practice and his status is day-to-day; Cam Jurgens is past protocol and could make his first start Sunday.
summary: Minter said Lamar Jackson was able to take some limited work in practice Wednesday as part of preparation, and that his availability is being handled day by day. He declined to detail Jackson's progress beyond saying the decision on playing from both sides will come when he is ready. Minter praised Jackson's attitude through the injury process, calling him a strong teammate who has seen improvement. On Cam Jurgens, Minter said the weekend helped him clear the protocol, and that his veteran experience across multiple offensive systems should help him be ready to contribute this week. Minter expects Jurgens to lift the offensive line, which could make his first start with the team on Sunday. On defense, Minter said the unit has improved on run defense, physicality and communication over recent weeks, but still needs more confidence and real-time adjustments. He said Cleveland's second-half approach, with loaded boxes and tight man coverage that neutralized outside zone runs, is something the team expects other opponents to copy. Minter framed the Bengals matchup as a chess match in which the defense must balance aggression with taking away Cincinnati's top-end receivers, and he called Dexter Lawrence a major factor for their defensive front. Minter also said the status of two players tied to roster and health decisions is a mix of both, with no timeline given.

title: Dave Canales on Panthers run defense: 'It’s not being talked about enough'
headline: Jaelan Phillips' hamstring is the key question for Sunday after a re-aggravation, Thomas Incoom is out with a calf injury, and Nick Hampton gets a look at OLB.
summary: Canales called Wednesday's work session productive, with full-speed throwing, timing, and special teams reps before the team scaled back. He said the staff used the session to get more players involved for the Detroit week and emphasized meetings, recovery, and work ethic over padded contact. Jaelan Phillips is dealing with the same hamstring that sidelined him earlier; he finished the last game, but the MRI findings mean the staff will manage him more carefully and he is still being evaluated. Canales said he would be surprised if Phillips were ready for the upcoming game, and he was not committing to Phillips for a short-week Thursday game. Thomas Incoom has a significant calf injury, will be out for a while with no firm timeline, and is being taken week to week; he is a big loss on special teams and at OLB. Nick Hampton, who had a strong camp before an injury, was brought back from the practice squad and will get an opportunity at OLB. Canales praised Tommy Tremble for his blocking and two touchdown catches, and he said Bryce Young's comfort is growing in the system as he approaches 50 career starts. He also said the run defense's recent success reflects scheme, effort, and execution, and that the group has improved its communication and understanding.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : October 21st, 2026
headline: Monken calls Jerry Jeudy a recent big-play producer and lists Harold Fannin Jr. and Denzel among the top-end targets, but says the passing game's inconsistency, not any one player, is limiting production.

On the passing game, he said the Harold Fannin Jr. and Deshaun Watson connection problem is not about Fannin specifically but about the offense becoming more consistent at throwing the football. He said the top-end targets, naming Fannin, Denzel and Jerry Jeudy, should see more production as drives get stronger. He praised Jeudy for coming up big the last few weeks. He also said he was encouraged by a player's frustration and effort to return from injury and said there is a good chance that player plays this week. Asked about the defense and sacks, he credited the defensive staff for keeping its scheme together. Monken also said he has not decided on the quarterback roster move and will decide closer to the deadline.

title: HC Sean Payton on facing the Cardinals’ defense: ‘We’re going to have to have the right answers'
headline: Payton says Coleman's possible return would help a deep backfield and the run game is still a work in progress; Elliss's injury is not season-ending, with an update due later in the week.
summary: Payton said the Cardinals' return-from-protocol player has been in good shape and training in the building, and that this week is about reacquainting him with practice and setting a pitch count before a decision for Sunday. He described Arizona's pressure-heavy defense as a challenge the Broncos must answer with the right plan, noting the Rams game showed how it can knock good offenses out of rhythm. He said the offense must improve on third downs and in finding open receivers, and that the second half of the last game was far from satisfying. On the run game, he called it a work in progress without assigning blame to the backs or the line. Taylor Rapp impressed him with smarts, toughness, and a clean transition. Payton said Jonah Coleman's possible return adds to a deep, talented room, and that Jonah Elliss's injury is not season-ending with an update coming later in the week. He praised Zach Allen's stamina, comparing it to players who play as fresh on snap 60 as on snap 1, and said J.K. Dobbins's versatility and extra reps factor into roster decisions.

title: Matt LaFleur on playing in Detroit: 'It's always a challenge'
headline: Josh Jacobs is back in walk-through and team work but his Sunday status is open, while Savion Williams is expected to take on the pre-snap motion and slot usage once handled by Jayden Reed.
summary: LaFleur said Thursday's session was a jog-through after the Sunday night game, with a fuller practice planned for the next day. He was unsure whether two full practices would get Josh Jacobs ready for Sunday and said they would work through it. He said he has a good feel for Jacobs' conditioning because Jacobs has been training with the strength staff, and that Jacobs can now join walk-through and team work. On Detroit, LaFleur called the Lions a physical, hard-hitting team that has allowed big plays, but he said they will be ready and the trip is always a challenge. He said the team prepares for road noise with simulated crowd noise and silent-count drills. On the offense, he said Savion Williams adds the element needed for pre-snap motion and slot usage, and that Bo Melton and others can handle some of it too. He said he prefers a multi-player approach so the role is covered if someone gets hurt. Asked about the offensive line and the drops, he said fundamentals and technique are the focus, with more individual time added after the personnel changes. He praised Jared Goff's ball security and called Jahmyr Gibbs a player who must be swarmed. He also said he believes in second chances for a player facing serious allegations who has shown remorse.

title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts at Vikings
headline: Steichen says TE Tyler Warren is progressing well but defers his Vikings status to the injury report; Minnesota's blitz-heavy defense is the main concern.
summary: Steichen opened by praising the Vikings as a talented 5-0 team with strong playmakers on offense and one of the league's best defenses. He said Minnesota's defense is highly multiple in its fronts, coverages, and blitzes, with a high blitz rate, and credited safety Harrison Smith as the quarterback of that unit. He emphasized that the Colts must communicate well, especially in a loud road environment. Asked about the team's seven straight road losses, he blamed execution, preparation, and handling crowd noise, and said practices will be loud to simulate it. On the blitz struggles, he said the problem isn't one player, citing some out-scouted looks and one-on-one wins and quicker releases as areas to fix. He said he meets with leaders weekly, including after Monday's meeting, and told them to keep working and stay committed. On Tyler Warren, he said the tight end is progressing really well but would defer to the injury report on his availability for Sunday. He also said he and the general manager talk through roster moves and actives throughout the week, and that the key is staying steady through losses.

title: Andy Reid: '[We] Look Forward to the Challenge of Playing the Seahawks' | Press Conference 10/21
headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) is improving day to day and Jaylon Moore is in the concussion protocol ahead of Seattle; Xavier Worthy is getting more targets as Mahomes spreads the ball.
summary: Reid opened by expressing sorrow over the passing of Alan Bailey, whom he called a favorite player and a good man. He said Jaylon Moore is in the concussion protocol and Rashee Rice is dealing with a hamstring injury, but Rice is improving daily. Reid said KC is looking forward to the challenge at Seattle, calling the Seahawks the defending champions and praising the 12th Man atmosphere. He described the Seahawks defense as the best in the business, with a sound scheme, good disguise, and a front that gives honest looks every snap. On Xavier Worthy, Reid said his recent production is less about breaking through and more about getting his number called as defenses roll coverage elsewhere, and that Mahomes is moving the ball around. He said Kenneth Walker III is level-headed and plays at one speed, so facing his former team shouldn't change much. Reid also expressed confidence that the kicker will work through his recent misses, and he was noncommittal about using Justin Fields in short-yardage situations, saying it's a thought he'd have to draw up.

title: Klint Kubiak on Tre Tucker: ‘Best conditioned athlete I’ve ever been around’

summary: Kubiak opened by saying Tonka Hemingway is in the protocol. He said the team's second-half struggles are partly mental and that starting the third quarter well is a point of emphasis, with practice reps built around it. He said Mendoza is doing more than asked, including extra solo work on the field. On the rookie class, he credited the scouting staff and said young players will have setbacks as they develop. He praised Tre Tucker's work and conditioning and said he has produced since April. He said Mike Washington Jr. has earned more reps and is growing in the passing game, but is not yet where he wants to be. He said the offense is still growing in year one, is moving in the right direction, and wants to improve running the ball in the red zone. He also said the team needs to stop playing close in the fourth quarter and finish games.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Oct 21 | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Douglas is back in practice but his return timeline runs through Friday; Malik Washington and Chris Bell get praise as the young receiving group develops.
summary: Hafley said the team is practicing with energy after the bye and that the group is fun to coach. Caleb Douglas was limited Monday and was set to practice Tuesday, with the staff reviewing how he feels before deciding on a game return by Friday. Hafley called Douglas's return a big boost to the offense and said he was a bright spot before his injury. He praised Chris Bell and Douglas as two young receivers with different strengths who could form a fun group, and called Malik Washington underrated. He said Kevin Coleman Jr. is improving even though the production has not arrived yet. On the pass rush, Hafley said the team needs more pressure and will work on both moving the quarterback off his spot and generating sacks. He also said the team is still learning its identity: it runs the ball well and plays physical run defense, but needs to develop more. Hafley previewed the Jets, praising Aaron Glenn and their physical roster, and said the game will be competitive.

title: Kevin O'Connell on Facing Colts in Week 7, Matt Daniels' Impact, Special Teams, Jake Golday & More
headline: T.J. Hockenson and Christian Darrisaw are trending toward playing Sunday, Jordan Addison is good to go, and Jordan Mason is a wait-and-see return from injury.
summary: O'Connell said T.J. Hockenson and Christian Darrisaw are both doing great and will work through the final phase of their return protocol in practice, and he is encouraged about their availability for the Colts game. Jordan Mason returns to practice this week, but the staff will evaluate his workload before deciding whether he can play Sunday. Jordan Addison is good to go, will practice fully, and is expected to play. O'Connell said the offense should look better with Mason and Hockenson healthy, praising Mason as a back who gets better as games go on and who pairs with Aaron Jones to keep the run game fresh. He emphasized that the team must avoid a sluggish start after the bye and that the 5-0 record does not guarantee execution. On special teams, he credited Matt Daniels for the unit's energy and cited Myles Price's visible impact, saying the unit is winning field position and making game-changing plays. He also described rookie Jake Golday's growth as a special teams player, and he said the staff wants to win the kicking game phase every week. Finally, he said he is open to trade-deadline conversations with Nolan if they can improve the team, while stressing confidence in the current roster and in the offseason plan.

title: Kellen Moore on Paris game, practice | Saints vs. Steelers 2026 NFL Week 7
headline: Cesar Ruiz (knee) missed practice but is day-to-day and traveled to Paris; Cameron Jordan won't practice this week with no firm return timeline, and Kaden Elliss returned to limited work.
summary: Kellen Moore opened by noting two absences from practice: Daniel Carlson (personal matter, still in the States and expected to arrive shortly) and Cesar Ruiz (knee). Ruiz traveled with the team, and Moore said his status will be taken day to day as the week progresses. Moore said most other players were limited or full participants and called practice a good, fun day despite rainstorms. On Jordan, he said Jordan won't practice this week, the team has no locked-in timeline for his return after the bye, and the staff deliberately avoided a hard target so he can get fully healthy. Moore said Kaden Elliss was on the field for some of practice, which is encouraging given how important Elliss has been to the defense. Moore described the trip as a unique opportunity, with players acclimating to the time zone and exploring Paris, and said the team will walk through Stade de France on Saturday. He framed Pittsburgh as a physical team with a sound offensive scheme led by a veteran quarterback, a big front that stops the run, and edge rushers who can wreck games, so the Saints must avoid giving up easy opportunities. He also reviewed the Giants and Raiders games, stressing ball security, third-down conversions, a more consistent run game, and preventing explosive plays.

title: Coach John Harbaugh on naming J.J. McCarthy starting QB
headline: J.J. McCarthy named starting QB for the Houston game, with Jameis Winston moved to backup; Harbaugh framed it as the go-forward plan, not a week-to-week call.
summary: Harbaugh announced that J.J. McCarthy will start at quarterback against Houston, with Jameis Winston as the backup and a third emergency quarterback behind him. He said the decision reflects what gives the offense its best chance, and that McCarthy's skill set fits what the team wants to do. He described this as the direction going forward, not a week-to-week arrangement, while adding that nothing in football is guaranteed. Harbaugh praised McCarthy's athleticism, arm talent, and quick grasp of the offense, and said the game plan has been tailored more toward his strengths. He called Winston one of the finest teammates and leaders he has been around, and said Winston has been helping McCarthy every step of the way. Harbaugh said the timing made more sense this week than last, when the team was set with Winston. He also said the offense's core concepts and blocking schemes remain the same despite the change in quarterback style. On Houston, he said they are healthier than early in the season, have added a receiver, and have two inside linebackers back, and he described their defense as aggressive but fundamentally sound under its new play-caller.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Oct. 21)
headline: DeShon Elliott is on a practice plan and McCarthy won't commit to his status; Pittsburgh is preparing for a Paris game on a normal seven-day week.
summary: McCarthy said the team had an abbreviated practice that day with a full session before traveling. He was asked about a player returning from injury and said he's been glad to have him back and that Aaron Rodgers is helping him with terminology, but he wouldn't say whether that player could play this week. On DeShon Elliott, who was called DeShawn in the question, McCarthy said he's on a practice plan, doing well, and eager to go, but he wouldn't confirm full-intensity work and said they'd see how the week goes. He said the locker room mood is business as usual and that the extra time before traveling was needed, while acknowledging that international travel is stressful. He described the Paris trip as different from his earlier international preseason trips because it's a regular-season game on a seven-day schedule, so sleep, hydration and travel planning matter. On the opponent, he said the offense is talented, that Kellen Moore will challenge them schematically, and that its perimeter players are playing well and spreading the ball around. He also discussed the value of receivers who run precise routes even when they aren't the target, stressing that details like quarterback training and protection timing matter. Asked about Moore, he said they know each other from their time in Dallas, that it's part of the competition, and that the opposing staff is young but off to a good start.

title: Todd Bowles on Baker Mayfield’s Practice: Progress | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield's thumb recovery is progressing, but his return is still undecided; coach will evaluate after Friday's practice.
summary: Bowles said Mayfield's return to practice was encouraging. Mayfield wore a glove on his throwing hand for the full session and reported it felt okay, and Bowles called his throwing effective once he warmed up. The coach will monitor how the thumb responds after Thursday and Friday, and he won't decide on Mayfield publicly until he sees him Friday. Reps are being split between Mayfield and Jalon Daniels, with each getting mental reps, and Bowles stressed that both understand the game plan. On timing, Bowles said medical staff had set a minimum of three games out for Mayfield, with the rest depending on how he felt. Antoine Winfield Jr. is still in a non-contact jersey and must practice before he can come off that designation, so Bowles is unsure whether he'll be ready this week. Bowles praised Carolina's offense under Brad, saying it has become more multiple and that Bryce Young is playing at a high level. On the defensive side, Bowles defended Calijah Kancey's stat line, saying he is in the backfield on nearly every play and the team needs to free him up and turn pressures into sacks. On the offense, Bowles said Chris Godwin is being used reasonably well, and the team is trying to scheme him open while still honoring coverages. Bowles also said the lack of downfield passing is partly by design to protect a young quarterback and limit turnovers, and partly because defenses take away the middle.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh says Jordan Elliott can't return under NFL gun policy; Alontae Taylor is being reset at corner; Cordale Flott praised for an interception; Kevin Winston is limited with a quad issue.
summary: Saleh opened with injury updates: John Franklin-Myers will sit today for normal maintenance, another unidentified player ("Taj") won't practice for maintenance, and a player ("Moose") is being activated from IR. Kevin Winston is back in practice on a limited basis with a quad injury, and Saleh said he'd be monitored in individual work before team work. On Jordan Elliott's gun incident in the parking lot, Saleh said the league and locker room are aware of the policy. He praised the organization and NFL for pausing and getting Elliott clinical help, argued the act looked like a call for help rather than a criminal act, and said Elliott deserves another chance. He said NFL rules keep Elliott from being on the team, and he would vouch for him to other teams. Saleh said he doesn't expect the incident to affect team chemistry and that the conversations had already happened internally. On Alontae Taylor, Saleh said he gave him a week to reset after his first time playing outside at corner, and noted Taylor had played corner at New Orleans and that the system includes more than just man coverage. On the interception, Saleh credited elite communication in the secondary and said Flott recognized the pre-snap formation and jumped the route.

topics.detail: Saleh said the Titans and NFL paused to get Elliott help after a gun was found in the parking lot. He said the locker room knows the policy and that the matter is handled internally. He did not elaborate on the details.
